The season, which was named "Walter Devoto", began on 5 February and ended on 30 October 2022 due to the [[2022 FIFA World Cup]] to be held in Qatar during November and December 2022.{{cite web |url=https://www.futbol.com.uy/Deportes/Campeonato-Uruguayo-Consejo-de-Liga-aprobo-el-formato-con-la-vuelta-del-Intermedio-uc809113 |title=Campeonato Uruguayo: Consejo de Liga aprobó el formato, con la vuelta del Intermedio |trans-title=Campeonato Uruguayo: League Council approved the format, with the return of the Intermedio |publisher=Futbol.com.uy |language=es |date=4 January 2022 |access-date=7 January 2022}}{{cite web |url=https://www.elobservador.com.uy/nota/la-auf-analiza-cambios-para-la-disputa-del-campeonato-uruguayo-2022-202112919050 |title=La AUF analiza cambios para la disputa del Campeonato Uruguayo 2022 |trans-title=AUF analyzes changes for the dispute of the 2022 Campeonato Uruguayo |publisher=El Observador |language=es |date=9 December 2021 |access-date=18 December 2021}} [[Club Nacional de Football|Nacional]] were the champions, winning their forty-ninth league title after placing first in the season's aggregate table and defeating [[Liverpool F.C. (Montevideo)|Liverpool]] in the semi-final match.{{cite web |url=https://www.futbol.com.uy/Deportes/Uruguayo-Nacional-con-doblete-de-Suarez-y-Gigliotti-vencio-4-1-a-Liverpool-y-es-campeon-uc836719 |title=Uruguayo: Nacional, con doblete de Suárez y Gigliotti, venció 4-1 a Liverpool y es campeón |trans-title=''Uruguayo'': Nacional, with braces by Suárez and Gigliotti, beat Liverpool 4–1 and are champions |publisher=Futbol.com.uy |language=es |date=30 October 2022 |access-date=30 October 2022}} [[Peñarol]] were the defending champions. ==Teams== 16 teams competed in the season: the top thirteen teams in the [[2021 Uruguayan Primera División season#Relegation|relegation table]] of the 2021 season as well as three promoted teams from the [[2021 Uruguayan Segunda División season|Segunda División]]. The three lowest placed teams in the relegation table of the 2021 season, [[C.A. Progreso|Progreso]], [[Sud América]], and [[C.S.D. Villa Española|Villa Española]], were relegated to the [[Uruguayan Segunda División|Segunda División]] for the 2022 season. They were replaced by [[Albion F.C.|Albion]], [[Danubio F.C.|Danubio]], and [[Defensor Sporting]], who were promoted from the Segunda División. Danubio and Defensor Sporting returned to the top flight after one season, whilst Albion played in Primera División for the first time in the professional era. On the other hand, both Sud América and Villa Española were relegated after one season, and Progreso returned to the second tier after four years.{{cite web |url=https://www.tenfield.com.uy/uruguayo-elsube-y-baja/ |title=Uruguayo: El sube y baja |trans-title=Uruguayo: The seesaw |publisher=Tenfield |language=es |date=14 December 2021 |access-date=18 December 2021}} ===Stadiums and locations=== {{location map+ |Uruguay |float=right |width=275 |caption=Locations of the 2022 season teams outside [[Montevideo]]. |places= {{location map~ |Uruguay |lat=-34.90 |long=-56.15 |label=
